$comment: PLATFORM MODULE (pack: platform) — MJ CORE usage residue (team requirement 2026-07-23; plan: plans/association-db/MJ-PLATFORM-RESIDUE-PLAN-2026-07-23.md). Seeds __mj APPLICATION data (never entity-definition rows — CodeGen owns those) so the instance looks actively used: 3 staff users, shared saved views (IsShared=1, visible to every viewer), reusable Approved queries (double as Skip entry points), RecordChange audit backfill DERIVED from timelines other packs already generate (issue resolutions, task completions, hero profile/period creation, stale-employer relationship edits — derive, never invent), plus per-staff Skip-style conversations, favorites, lists, notifications (demos log in as a staff persona — team ruling 2026-07-23). All enum values and column shapes verified against a real v5.45 __mj schema incl. CHECK constraints (F9): ConversationDetail.Role is 'User'|'AI', List.RefreshMode 'Sync'|'Additive', Query.Status 'Approved', RecordChange Type/Source/Status value lists. EnvironmentID and SQLDialectID are OMITTED on insert — their column DEFAULTs are the Default environment / T-SQL dialect constants. Conversation texts may embed {N:FACT} / {HERO:memberNumber} tokens — the generator substitutes COMPUTED numbers from the same world, so every claim in a seeded transcript is true for the build.

queries.name: Why we lose members, by year
queries.userQuestion: What reasons do members give for leaving, and how has that changed?
queries.description: Terminal memberships grouped by year and recorded reason — the two ways a membership ends, side by side.
queries.sql: SELECT YEAR(EndDate) AS EndYear, Status, CancellationReason, COUNT(*) AS Memberships FROM [morecheese_members].[vwMembershipPeriods] WHERE Status IN ('Lapsed','Cancelled') GROUP BY YEAR(EndDate), Status, CancellationReason ORDER BY EndYear DESC, Memberships DESC

queries.name: Attendance rate by event format
queries.userQuestion: Which event formats do people actually turn up to?
queries.description: Registrations and attendance per event type and year — the no-show rate that tells you whether a format is working.
queries.sql: SELECT e.EventType, YEAR(e.EventDate) AS EventYear, COUNT(*) AS Registrations, SUM(CASE WHEN r.Attended = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Attended FROM [morecheese_events].[vwEventRegistrations] r JOIN [morecheese_events].[vwEvents] e ON e.ID = r.EventID GROUP BY e.EventType, YEAR(e.EventDate) ORDER BY EventYear DESC, e.EventType

queries.name: Dues revenue by tier and year
queries.userQuestion: How much dues revenue does each membership tier bring in each year?
queries.description: Posted dues orders rolled up by tier and year — the revenue view behind any pricing conversation.
queries.sql: SELECT p.MembershipTier, YEAR(p.StartDate) AS PeriodYear, COUNT(*) AS Memberships, SUM(p.DuesAmount) AS DuesBilled FROM [morecheese_members].[vwMembershipPeriods] p GROUP BY p.MembershipTier, YEAR(p.StartDate) ORDER BY PeriodYear DESC, DuesBilled DESC

queries.name: Committee service load
queries.userQuestion: Who carries the committee workload, and which committees are thin?
queries.description: Seats per committee and term, with officer counts — surfaces both the over-committed volunteers and the committees that struggle to fill.
queries.sql: SELECT c.Name AS Committee, t.Name AS Term, COUNT(*) AS Seats FROM [__mj_BizAppsCommittees].[vwMemberships] m JOIN [__mj_BizAppsCommittees].[vwTerms] t ON t.ID = m.TermID JOIN [__mj_BizAppsCommittees].[vwCommittees] c ON c.ID = t.CommitteeID GROUP BY c.Name, t.Name ORDER BY c.Name, t.Name DESC

queries.name: Members by segment and region
queries.userQuestion: How are our members distributed across segments and regions?
queries.description: Member profile counts grouped by segment and region.
queries.sql: SELECT Segment, Region, COUNT(*) AS Members FROM [morecheese_members].[vwMemberProfiles] GROUP BY Segment, Region ORDER BY Members DESC

queries.name: Open issues by type and severity
queries.userQuestion: What support issues are open right now, and how severe are they?
queries.description: Open ticket counts by issue type and severity.
queries.sql: SELECT IssueType, Severity, COUNT(*) AS OpenIssues FROM [__mj_BizAppsIssues].[vwIssues] WHERE Status NOT IN ('Resolved','Closed') GROUP BY IssueType, Severity ORDER BY OpenIssues DESC

queries.name: Lapsed memberships by year
queries.userQuestion: How many memberships lapsed each year?
queries.description: Lapse counts by the year the membership period ended.
queries.sql: SELECT YEAR(EndDate) AS YearEnded, COUNT(*) AS Lapsed FROM [morecheese_members].[vwMembershipPeriods] WHERE Status='Lapsed' GROUP BY YEAR(EndDate) ORDER BY YearEnded

turns.text: Which members look at risk of not renewing this cycle?

Looking across renewal status, satisfaction and open support items: {N:PENDING_RENEWALS} memberships are pending renewal right now, and {N:LAPSED_2025} lapsed during 2025. The clearest individual risk signal is {HERO:ICF-000105} — declining survey scores across three conferences, reduced event participation, and an open billing dispute that also has an unanswered secure-message thread. I'd prioritize resolving the billing issue before the renewal conversation.
What about billing issues generally — how many are open?

There are {N:OPEN_BILLING} open billing issues. Members with an unresolved billing dispute at renewal time lapse at a visibly higher rate in this dataset, so the open ones are worth triaging this week.
Give me a quick read on the membership base composition.

The federation currently has {N:MEMBER_COUNT} member profiles. The largest segment is {N:TOP_SEGMENT} with {N:TOP_SEGMENT_COUNT} members. I saved the full segment-by-region breakdown as the reusable query "Members by segment and region" if you want the complete table.
How did attendance look for the most recent annual conference?

The {N:CONF_YEAR} conference drew {N:CONF_REGS} registrations, of which {N:CONF_ATTENDED} attended — a {N:CONF_ATTEND_PCT}% attendance rate. No-shows are concentrated in first-time registrants, which matches the historical pattern in this dataset.
